overview: The CC Park Commission manages the permitting, maintenance, and policy for Medford's parks, pools, and recreational facilities. The body reviews seasonal field and court requests from local sports leagues, schools, and private organizations to ensure fair use of city resources. Its work spans from early 2023 through late 2026, covering infrastructure projects like flood mitigation and community garden expansions. As of the most recent meetings, the commission is shifting focus toward reviewing long-term fee structures, pavilion reservation policies, and field priorities for youth sports.

threads.name: Athletic Field and Court Permitting
threads.summary: The commission regularly reviews and approves permits for a variety of sports including youth soccer, softball, tennis, and ultimate frisbee. Requests are often contingent on Department of Public Works field readiness and coordination between different leagues to avoid scheduling conflicts. In several instances, permits were tabled or held until applicant representatives could attend meetings or provide specific insurance documentation. By late 2026, the body began planning a broader review of field priorities for youth sports.

citations.title: Permit Application: Medford Youth Girls Softball
citations.label: M01#7

threads.name: Pickleball Policy and Facilities
threads.summary: Early in 2023, the commission reviewed citywide survey results and considered expanding courts at Duggar Park, though the proposal was initially tabled for funding confirmation. The body also handled requests for memorial plaques at new pickleball courts, deferring decisions until construction progress was made. By 2026, the commission established specific tournament policies for the Carr Park courts, including a daily fee and restrictions on signage.

threads.name: Facility Access and Fee Policies
threads.summary: The commission manages access rules and fees for city-managed facilities like Tufts Pool and Wright's Pond. In 2023, the body approved eliminating daily drop-in passes for non-residents at Tufts Pool to prioritize resident access. More recently, the commission has taken up discussions regarding vehicle stickers and walking passes for Wright's Pond. The body also reviews financial matters such as permit revenue fluctuations and the allocation of Community Preservation Act funds.

citations.title: Tufts Pool Non-Resident Daily Fee Policy
citations.label: M01#11

threads.name: Park Infrastructure and Improvements
threads.summary: The commission oversees physical changes to park land, including flood mitigation designs and garden expansions. In 2026, consultants presented conceptual designs for Tufts Park that included underground storage to manage flooding and potential reorientation of softball fields. During the same period, the body approved adding ten new beds to the community garden at Tufts Park. Other projects include tree planting and soil preparation efforts at College Grove.

citations.title: College Grove Tree Planting and Celebration
citations.label: M05#1

threads.name: Community Events and Public Art
threads.summary: Beyond athletic leagues, the commission reviews permits for one-time community events ranging from school fundraisers to cultural festivals. It has approved the relocation of traveling art exhibits to Brooks Park and handled logistics for the United India Summer Fest. The body also manages requests for donations, such as providing pond and pool passes to local school PTOs for fundraising raffles.

threads.name: Technology and Contractual Agreements
threads.summary: The commission has explored technological upgrades for court management, specifically through a contract with the USTA. A proposal for smart access to courts was tabled in late 2025 to allow for legal review by the City Solicitor. The commission sought to resolve concerns from city and USTA legal teams before proceeding with the project.

periods.narrative: This period focused on establishing seasonal permit cycles for local sports and revising residency requirements for pool access.
During this term, the commission managed fall sports permitting and authorized the installation of public art in city parks.
Recent work has shifted toward large-scale infrastructure designs for flood mitigation and the formalization of tournament fees.
